notes: rounds/tester.py checks everything in the view: unavailable() refuses a non-Open round or a superseded build for GET and again under the round lock for POST, own_result reads the tester's row, and the POST refuses a submitted one; services.save_result only writes, with update_or_create keyed by tester, case and build. M1 drops the tester filter in own_result and keys the service's update_or_create on case and build (the tester goes in create_defaults), so another tester's draft is shown and overwritten; M3 lets unavailable() pass a Closed round; M4 removes the POST check, shows the form for a submitted result (the GET always builds one) and prints its real status there, and a save after submission turns it back into a draft because the service sets submitted_at from the action. ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); M5 raises only ObservationField's max_length, so its message still says 2000. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_result to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
